key_insight: Motile microorganisms can self-organize into bioconvective plumes that enhance heat and mass transfer, offering a bio-inspired route to low-carbon thermal management.
engineering_relevance: Bioconvection could reduce pumping energy and strengthen cooling performance in hybrid systems for data centers, electronics, and other heat-intensive technologies.
method: Reviewed natural and laboratory studies of bioconvection and microorganism-driven hydrodynamics.
Synthesized pattern formation, thermofluidic transport, and thermal-management mechanisms.
Assessed feasibility using quantitative thermal-performance analysis and non-dimensional numbers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative analyses comparing thermal performance and framing the results with relevant non-dimensional metrics, but it does not present new experimental data.
watch_item: Practical deployment remains limited by microbial stability, material compatibility, controllability, scalability, and integration with existing cooling hardware.
paper_title: Engineering Collective Microbial Dynamics for Sustainable Thermal Management
